evidence: Flat directory structure with all modules in a single top-level package (alluka.modules) showing cohesive ownership
All modules share the same runtime process and depend on shared state (dispatcher, updater, database session, config)
Centralized event dispatching via Telegram.ext (sync) and Telethon (async) event handlers
SQL-based persistence layer using shared SQLAlchemy session and BASE pattern across all modules
Shared utilities (helper_funcs) used across modules, with tight integration and circular dependencies (e.g., connection_status calling connection module)
No explicit service boundaries or inter-process communication; all functionality logically grouped by domain (e.g., admin, warns, notes)
Low number of packages (4), low average fan-out (~4.4), and shallow depth (5) consistent with a cohesive monolith
Modules directly import from each other (e.g., antiflood imports chat_status, sql), indicating tight coupling and shared memory space
risks: Tight coupling between modules impedes independent deployment and testing
Shared database session and global state (dispatcher, updater) creates hidden dependencies and testability issues
Circular import potential (e.g., chat_status depending on connection module while connection depends on chat_status)
Lack of clear boundaries makes scalability and maintainability harder as codebase grows
